meanings.note: Street and house number. Common masculine noun meaning 'address' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll give the address: seven Sadovaya Street.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

гнать.gloss: to chase away, to drive out

meanings.en: to chase away, to drive away
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to chase away, to drive out', paired with 'прогнать'.

examples.trans: Why are you chasing him away?

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не гони меня. Я знаю, что я виноват.
examples.trans: Please, don't chase me away. I know it's my fault.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: что и требовалось доказать = Q.E.D., which is what needed to be proved

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.
+ genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'because of; from behind' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: перед + instrumental: before someone

examples.text: Ну что ты, Филиппович. Я же извинился.
examples.trans: Oh, come on, Filippovich. I said sorry, didn't I?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pile, heap, bunch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He has a pile of money.
A pile of papers lay on the table.

examples.text: Допустим, у губернатора есть куча денег.
examples.trans: Let's suppose the governor has a pile of money.

meanings.note: In indirect questions. Core Russian part meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: что ли = or what, I suppose
meanings.note: Colloquial tag. Core Russian part meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

отвезти.gloss: to drive, to take (someone somewhere by vehicle)

meanings.en: to take, to drive (someone to a place)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'везти'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drive, to take (someone somewhere by vehicle)', paired with 'отвозить'.

examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

examples.text: Вот это дело! Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Now we're talking! Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: In 'по поводу' + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'along; by; about' in everyday speech.
+ dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'along; by; about' in everyday speech.
'по телефону'. Core Russian prep meaning 'along; by; about' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to send (something or someone to the speaker)
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'слать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to send (here)', paired with 'присылать'.

examples.trans: They sent me a free lawyer.

examples.text: Послушайте, здесь ошибка. Ко мне прислали бесплатного адвоката. В чём дело?
examples.trans: Listen, there's a mistake here. They sent me a free lawyer. What's going on?

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'спорить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lose a bet'.

examples.trans: You lost the bet. Five thousand?

examples.text: Ты же вчера при всех честно проспорил мне пять тысяч!
examples.trans: Yesterday in front of everyone you fairly lost a five-thousand-ruble bet to me!

examples.text: Сеня боялся проспорить Феде целую коробку дорогих сигар.
examples.trans: Senya was afraid of losing a whole box of expensive cigars in a bet to Fedya.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пять рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: Inanimate masculine noun. Common masculine noun meaning 'belt, strap' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A leather strap on the watch.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не затягивайте ремень слишком сильно.
examples.trans: Please do not tighten the strap too tightly.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to argue, to dispute', paired with 'поспорить'.

examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

examples.text: Это кошмар, я не спорю. Но зачем на видео снимать?
examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue. But why film it on video?

meanings.note: A whole portion; completed action. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat (up)', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: 'mum will kill me' = I'll be in big trouble

examples.trans: Do you want to kill me?

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
